items.t: Adults: major depressive disorder; diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain; generalised anxiety disorder.

src.q: Treatment of major depressive disorder. Treatment of diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain. Treatment of generalised anxiety disorder. Duloxetine is indicated in adults.
Treatment of major depressive disorder. Treatment of diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain. Treatment of generalised anxiety disorder.

items.t: Adults only. Should not be used under 18 years for major depressive disorder; safety and efficacy not established for other paediatric uses.

src.q: Duloxetine should not be used in children and adolescents under the age of 18 years for the treatment of major depressive disorder because of safety and efficacy concerns

items.t: Duloxetine is marketed under different names for several indications (including stress urinary incontinence): avoid using more than one duloxetine product at the same time.

src.q: The use of more than one of these products concomitantly should be avoided.

items.t: 60 mg once daily, with or without food (start and maintenance). Doses up to 120 mg/day studied for safety, but no evidence that non-responders benefit from increases. Response usually in 2 to 4 weeks; continue several months after response.

src.q: The starting and recommended maintenance dose is 60 mg once daily with or without food.
there is no clinical evidence suggesting that patients not responding to the initial recommended dose may benefit from dose up-titrations
Therapeutic response is usually seen after 2-4 weeks of treatment.

items.t: Start 30 mg once daily; if response is insufficient increase to 60 mg (usual maintenance). With co-morbid depression start and maintain 60 mg. 90 mg or 120 mg may be considered if response to 60 mg is insufficient.

src.q: The recommended starting dose in patients with generalised anxiety disorder is 30 mg once daily with or without food.
In patients with insufficient response, the dose should be increased to 60 mg, which is the usual maintenance dose in most patients.
In patients with insufficient response to 60 mg, escalation up to 90 mg or 120 mg may therefore be considered.

items.t: 60 mg daily, with or without food. Some may benefit from up to 120 mg/day in evenly divided doses. Assess response after 2 months; reassess benefit at least every 3 months.

src.q: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathic Pain The starting and recommended maintenance dose is 60 mg daily with or without food.
up to a maximum dose of 120 mg per day administered in evenly divided doses
Response to treatment should be evaluated after 2 months.
The therapeutic benefit should be reassessed regularly (at least every three months)

items.t: Elderly: no dose change for age alone; caution, especially with 120 mg/day for depression or anxiety (limited data).

src.q: No dosage adjustment is recommended for elderly patients solely on the basis of age.
caution should be exercised when treating the elderly, especially with duloxetine 120 mg per day

items.t: Stopping: avoid abrupt withdrawal; reduce gradually over at least 1 to 2 weeks (4.2), no less than 2 weeks (4.4). If intolerable symptoms, resume the previous dose and taper more slowly.

src.q: When stopping treatment with duloxetine the dose should be gradually reduced over a period of at least one to two weeks in order to reduce the risk of withdrawal reactions
duloxetine should be gradually tapered when discontinuing treatment over a period of no less than 2 weeks, according to the patient's needs

items.t: Not for use under 18 years. Major depressive disorder: should not be used (safety and efficacy concerns). Generalised anxiety disorder aged 7 to 17: safety and efficacy not established. Neuropathic pain: not studied.

src.q: Duloxetine should not be used in children and adolescents under the age of 18 years for the treatment of major depressive disorder because of safety and efficacy concerns
The safety and efficacy of duloxetine for the treatment of generalised anxiety disorder in paediatric patients aged 7-17 years have not been established.

src.q: Concomitant use of duloxetine with non-selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) is contraindicated

src.q: Duloxetine should not be used in combination with fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin or enoxacin (i.e. potent CYP1A2 inhibitors), since the combination results in elevated plasma concentrations of duloxetine

items.t: Severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min).

items.t: Starting duloxetine in uncontrolled hypertension (risk of hypertensive crisis).

items.t: Blood pressure and heart rate: rises and hypertensive crisis reported, especially with pre-existing hypertension. Monitor BP in hypertension or other cardiac disease, especially in the first month. If BP stays raised, reduce the dose or taper off.

src.q: Cases of hypertensive crisis have been reported with duloxetine, especially in patients with pre-existing hypertension.
in patients with known hypertension and/or other cardiac disease, blood pressure monitoring is recommended, especially during the first month of treatment
either dose reduction or gradual discontinuation should be considered

items.t: Serotonin syndrome / NMS, especially with other serotonergic drugs, MAOIs, antipsychotics or other dopamine antagonists: if combined use is needed, observe carefully at start and after dose increases. St John's wort: adverse reactions may be more common.

src.q: particularly with concomitant use of other serotonergic agents (including SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants or triptans)
careful observation of the patient is advised, particularly during treatment initiation and dose increases
Adverse reactions may be more common during concomitant use of duloxetine and herbal preparations containing St John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum).

items.t: Mania, bipolar disorder or seizures: use with caution. Raised intraocular pressure or risk of acute angle-closure glaucoma: caution (mydriasis).

src.q: Duloxetine should be used with caution in patients with a history of mania or a diagnosis of bipolar disorder, and/or seizures.
caution should be used when prescribing duloxetine to patients with increased intraocular pressure, or those at risk of acute narrow-angle glaucoma

items.t: Bleeding (ecchymoses, purpura, GI haemorrhage): caution with anticoagulants, drugs affecting platelets (e.g. NSAIDs, aspirin) and bleeding tendencies. May increase postpartum haemorrhage.

src.q: Caution is advised in patients taking anticoagulants and/or medicinal products known to affect platelet function (e.g. NSAIDs or acetylsalicylic acid (ASA)) and in patients with known bleeding tendencies.
Duloxetine may increase the risk of postpartum haemorrhage

items.t: Hyponatraemia (sometimes <110 mmol/L), often SIADH, mostly in the elderly: caution in elderly, cirrhotic or dehydrated patients and those on diuretics.

src.q: Caution is required in patients at increased risk for hyponatraemia, such as elderly, cirrhotic or dehydrated patients or patients treated with diuretics.

items.t: Suicidal thoughts and clinical worsening: monitor closely until improvement, especially early in treatment and after dose changes; higher risk under 25 years.

src.q: patients should be closely monitored until such improvement occurs
increased risk of suicidal behaviour with antidepressants compared to placebo in patients less than 25 years old

items.t: Liver injury (severe enzyme rises, hepatitis, jaundice), mostly in the first months: use with caution with other medicines associated with liver injury.

src.q: Cases of liver injury, including severe elevations of liver enzymes (>10 times upper limit of normal), hepatitis and jaundice have been reported with duloxetine
Duloxetine should be used with caution in patients treated with other medicinal products associated with hepatic injury.

items.t: Sexual dysfunction may occur and may continue after stopping. Akathisia may occur in early weeks; increasing the dose may be harmful.

src.q: There have been reports of long-lasting sexual dysfunction where the symptoms have continued despite discontinuation of SSRIs/SNRIs.
In patients who develop these symptoms, increasing the dose may be detrimental.

items.t: One UK SmPC: contains sucrose; patients with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrose-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: Non-selective irreversible MAOIs: contraindicated; wait 14 days after an MAOI and at least 5 days after duloxetine before an MAOI. Moclobemide: not recommended. Linezolid: should not be given.

src.q: duloxetine should not be used in combination with non-selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or within at least 14 days of discontinuing treatment with an MAOI
at least 5 days should be allowed after stopping duloxetine before starting an MAOI
The concomitant use of duloxetine with selective, reversible MAOIs, like moclobemide, is not recommended

items.t: Potent CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin, enoxacin): contraindicated. Fluvoxamine raised duloxetine AUC 6-fold.

src.q: duloxetine should not be administered in combination with potent inhibitors of CYP1A2 like fluvoxamine

items.t: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics such as amitriptyline, moclobemide, linezolid, St John's wort, triptans, tramadol, pethidine, tryptophan): caution (serotonin syndrome).

src.q: Duloxetine is a moderate inhibitor of CYP2D6.

items.t: Smoking: smokers have almost 50% lower duloxetine levels. Aluminium/magnesium antacids and famotidine: no significant effect.

src.q: smokers have almost 50% lower plasma concentrations of duloxetine compared with non-smokers

items.t: Mild or moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30 to 80 mL/min): no dose change. Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): contraindicated.

MHRA: weigh PPH risk against individual bleeding/thrombotic risk.
